content:
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are all about what's on the inside. The new health sensor system is the biggest feature, bringing the biggest leap in health tracking for Apple Watch in years.

I've been using the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 for the past week, and here's everything you need to know.

  • Apple Watch Series 12 starts at $390 (down from $399)
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4 in Black starts at $780 (down from $799)

Design

The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 look the same as the previous generation. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 again comes in two titanium color options: Natural and Black, and my review unit is the Natural version.

For Apple Watch Series 12, the design highlights are mostly in the colors and materials.

First, there's a small change to the dimensions of Apple Watch Series 12. Apple's tech specs page notes that the screen's display area is about 2% smaller than Series 10 and Series 11, but the overall pixel count is unchanged. With the slight reduction in display area, the Series 12 case is about 1mm wider than the previous model.

In practice, you can't feel these differences at all, and the Apple Watch's screen still extends nearly to the edge of the case. Given the new health sensor system (more on that below), it's impressive that Apple was still able to maintain this design.

Apple Watch Series 12 is available in three materials: aluminum, titanium, and ceramic.

The aluminum version comes in four colors: Deep Bronze, Light Gold, Black, and Space Gray. The aluminum version's cover glass has also been upgraded from Ion-X to Ceramic Shield 2.

My Apple Watch Series 12 review unit is the Black aluminum version. Compared to last year's glossy Jet Black aluminum case, this year's black Series 12 has a matte finish. I personally preferred the look of Jet Black, but I understand Apple changes the design style each year and glossy black will likely return at some point.

I got to see all the colors of the Series 12 aluminum in person last week at Apple's event, and the standout for me was Deep Bronze. It's an elegant color unlike any previous aluminum Apple Watch. Light Gold is also a great choice for those who like gold. There's no silver aluminum Series 12, but Space Gray is a fairly light shade, and I think most people will consider it a silver alternative.

Apple Watch Series 12 in titanium comes in two colors: Gold and Natural. For comparison, Series 11 titanium came in Natural, Gold, and Slate.

The Gold color is a head-turner. It looks very different from last year's Gold from the outside, and I think Apple's intent is clear: make the titanium Series 12 look as much like real gold as possible without using actual gold. Everyone's impression of "real gold" is different, but in my eyes, Apple did an excellent job with the Gold titanium Series 12.

And finally, there's the Apple Watch Series 12 in ceramic, available in two colors: Midnight Blue and Pearl White. The last time Apple offered a ceramic watch was 2019 with the Series 5, and it quickly became a fan favorite.

I only had a few minutes with the ceramic Series 12 at last week's Apple event. Midnight Blue is nice, but Pearl White caught my eye right away. Depending on the light, it's not the pure white of the Series 5, but rather a soft, off-white hue.

Health tracking

The biggest change to Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 is the all-new health sensor system, which I think is the biggest health feature upgrade for Apple Watch in years.

First, the sensor hardware has been completely redesigned. Apple highlights three things:

  • The electrode contact area is larger, but the sensor itself isn't any bigger, leading to better skin contact during ECG readings.
  • The photodiodes have been redesigned and arranged in a ring to capture more reflected light.
  • The green LEDs are larger, making readings more reliable when you're moving around, as well as more power-efficient.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are able to take more accurate and more frequent background heart rate measurements, meaning they read heart rate data more often outside of workouts.

Previous Apple Watch models primarily attempted to read background heart rate every five minutes when you were at rest.

Apple says the new health sensor system delivers "the most accurate heart rate sensing of any wearable." In a study with over 1,000 participants, Apple says the Series 12 was statistically better than every competitor wearable they tested for overall accuracy during exercise and daily activities.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 see a major improvement: they now read your heart rate every five seconds, whether you're moving or at rest. Such high-frequency and accurate heart rate readings unlock more data and insights.

Previous Apple Watch models measured heart rate every five minutes at rest, which had an inherent blind spot: they might completely miss moments when your heart rate rises outside of exercise, or only randomly capture one or two data points in between those moments.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 not only take more readings, but also measure during your movement. You can clearly see the heart rate impact of activities like carrying groceries, doing yard work, or shoveling snow.

Apple has also added several new ways to view heart rate data. First, the Heart Rate app on Apple Watch has been redesigned, and now shows a graph of your real-time heart rate and readings from the past two minutes.

There are also two new heart rate complications for the watch face, giving you an at-a-glance look at your real-time heart rate.

After using Series 12 and Ultra 4 for a week, I found these new additions to be very illuminating, giving me a better understanding of how small things in daily life impact my heart rate. For example, I could visually see the impact of an afternoon coffee or a stressful moment at work.

In addition to providing more raw data, Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 also actively leverage more frequent heart rate readings to power new features and improvements.

First, Apple says this data leads to more accurate calorie estimates. I haven't noticed a big change in my own data, but maybe more than a week of wear will make it clearer.

I was hoping that more frequent heart rate measurements might improve automatic workout detection, but in my testing so far, that doesn't seem to be the case.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 now sample heart rate variability (HRV) at a higher rate. Previously, HRV was measured every two hours, but the new Apple Watch models can measure as frequently as every five minutes when at rest.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 also add Recovery HRV tracking, which is best for identifying daily stress and fatigue signals. The new Apple Watch models also continue to measure overall HRV, which has long been useful for identifying broader health signals.

Additionally, Apple has integrated Recovery HRV measurement into the overnight Vitals feature.

Vitals

Speaking of Vitals, Apple has made several changes to the overall Vitals experience on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. First, Vitals now has a daytime view mode.

Previously, Vitals was only an overnight report that you saw in the morning. The daytime view shows your daytime heart rate and HRV, with the idea being that you don't have to wait for the overnight Vitals report to know if something is off.

Vitals now also categorizes your metrics into four groups: Out of Range, Below Typical, Typical, or Strong. Compared to the previous two-tier classification of only Typical or Out of Range, this provides more granular layering.

I really love the Vitals app on Apple Watch, and I'm glad to see Apple make meaningful improvements with the Series 12 and Ultra 4. It's detected illness more than once before I've even gotten sick.

The new daytime view only covers two metrics for now, so it will need more testing to see how useful it is. However, some of the Vitals improvements are definitely nice, leveraging the more frequent heart rate and HRV measurements that Series 12 and Ultra 4 bring.

Readiness

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 offer a new Readiness score, aiming to consolidate all the data Apple Watch knows into a single score.

Apple says Readiness takes into account your recent activity, training load, Vitals, and sleep score. The Readiness score also updates throughout the day based on new data like naps, activity, and daytime heart rate, so it dynamically adjusts as new data comes in.

You can view your Readiness score in the Readiness app on Apple Watch or in the Fitness app on iPhone. Readiness is also available in the beta version of the redesigned Health app.

Apple Watch's main competitors have offered similar scores for years, including Whoop (Whoop Recovery) and Oura (Ready Score). Apple adding its own Readiness feature with Series 12 and Ultra 4 is the most direct response to these competitors yet.

I've worn an Oura Ring for the past year, mainly for its Ready Score. I appreciate being able to consolidate multiple different metrics into a single simple number that's clearly visible every morning. I've always felt that the Apple Watch software experience was missing this piece, and I'm glad Apple has now adopted a similar approach.

The Apple Watch Readiness score requires a week of sleep data, and my review unit has only been on my wrist for exactly a week, so I've only gotten a single Readiness score so far and it's too early to judge how useful Apple's feature is.

Looking at the types of data Apple uses to calculate Readiness, I'm optimistic about it. I also think Apple is right to use a 0-10 scale rather than Oura's 0-100 scale. Here's the Readiness score range from Apple:

  • 0-1: Recover
  • 2-4: Pace Yourself
  • 5-7: Ready
  • 8-10: Go For It

These score ranges look pretty intuitive and may be more practical than Oura's scores and sometimes preachy (or passive-aggressive) recommendations. Looking forward to testing over the coming weeks and comparing directly with Oura's scores.

For comparison, on a day when my Apple Watch Readiness score was 8/10, my Oura Ring was 85/100.

I also like that Readiness shows you which factors are pulling your score up or down, whether it's sleep, activity, or overnight Vitals, and you can tap in for more details.

Performance

Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Apple Watch Series 12 both feature Apple's new S11 chip, which Apple describes as "the most powerful wearable chip ever."

The S11 is the first truly new chip for Apple Watch since the S9 in the Series 9 back in 2023. The S10 chip in Series 10 was just a thinner packaged version of the same architecture, and last year's model had no new chip at all.

Apple emphasizes that the new S11 chip contains CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine components derived from the iPhone 18 Pro's A20 Pro chip. The chip reportedly also doubles Apple Watch's RAM from 2GB to 4GB.

The S11 has another standout feature: a new always-on processor capable of handling complex workloads without engaging the main chip. Inside is a secure exclave, a hardware-isolated space used to keep Audio Intelligence microphone data private and secure.

Apple says the S11 chip, combined with the always-on processor, plays a major role in several features on the Series 12 and Ultra 4:

  • Powering more frequent heart rate readings with the new health sensor system.
  • Supporting Audio Intelligence features like Siri Recap (more on that below).
  • Running a redesigned pedometer model that Apple claims is more accurate, even when your arm isn't moving (e.g., pushing a stroller).

Compared to my Apple Watch Ultra 3, the Ultra 4 and Series 12 feel faster when opening new apps, scrolling through menus, and performing basic Siri AI operations. But for me, the standout is powering the new health features mentioned above.

Battery life

Apple Watch Series 12 features a slightly larger battery, combined with more power efficiency from the health sensor system and S11 chip. Here are Apple's battery life claims for the Series 12:

  • 24 hours of general use (same as Series 11)
  • 38 hours in Low Power Mode (same as Series 11)
  • 10 hours of outdoor workout, up 2 hours

Apple also highlights faster charging speeds in specific scenarios:

  • 5 minutes of charging provides up to 10 hours of sleep tracking
  • 15 minutes of charging provides up to 12 hours of battery life
  • Approximately 30 minutes to charge to 80% (same as previous generation)

What impressed me most about the Series 12 in my testing were the first two. Apple Watch is increasingly focused on sleep tracking, and being able to quickly top up the battery before bed is really important.

Apple Watch Ultra 4 also features a larger battery, and Apple says:

  • 50 hours of general use, up from 42 hours on Ultra 3
  • 84 hours in Low Power Mode, up from 72 hours on Ultra 3
  • Workouts: 18 hours standard (up from 14 hours), 25 hours extended (up from 20 hours), and 45 hours longest extended
  • 15 minutes of charging provides up to 18 hours of battery life, up from 12 hours on Ultra 3

In my testing, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 indeed lived up to Apple's battery life claims. In a real-world test, I fully charged it around 8 PM on Sunday night, and didn't put it back on the charger until 8 PM on Tuesday night. That's 48 hours on a single charge, including 90 minutes of workout tracking, 3 hours away from my iPhone, and two nights of sleep tracking.

Other details

  • There's a new Steps watch face complication that updates your step count in real time, and I love this feature.
  • Apple has redesigned the Ocean Band for Apple Watch Ultra with a translucent silicone material, available in three colors: translucent gray, translucent seaweed green, and translucent black. In addition to looking different, the new Ocean Band is also lighter on the wrist.
  • There's a new Siri Modular watch face, which is also backward compatible. Zac has a detailed write-up here.

More features are on the way

This is just the beginning of new features for Apple Watch this year.

First, Apple is developing a completely redesigned Health app, adding new tabs like Longevity and metrics like Health Age. I'm really looking forward to trying out the new Health app. Apple says the new Health app will launch later this year via a software update, and a beta has opened up as of Wednesday afternoon.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 will get Audio Intelligence features later this year, including Live Rewind and Siri Recap.

Live Rewind lets you double-press the Digital Crown to review the last 15 seconds of conversation as text. Siri Recap generates high-level summaries of conversations for you to review later. Apple says both features will launch in beta later this year. The company has also established detailed privacy policies for these features.

With the rollout of Siri AI, Siri Recap and Live Rewind are Apple's biggest steps yet in turning Apple Watch into a full-fledged AI wearable, and I'm excited to see how this area develops.

9to5Mac Take

Who should upgrade to Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4? I think this is one of the most substantial upgrades in years. If you're on a Series 9 or Ultra 2 (or older), I'd seriously consider upgrading. If you already have a newer Apple Watch, it depends on how much you value the new health features.

On the surface, Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 might seem like minor changes. They haven't been redesigned (although the new color and material options are great).

Instead, it's the upgrades on the inside that make Series 12 and Ultra 4 so interesting. Apple has focused on strengthening what Apple Watch already does best: being a companion you wear all the time, monitoring your heart, sleep, and activity. And of course, helping you stay connected with friends, family, and the outside world.

The new health sensor system is the foundation for all of the above, fundamentally changing how much your Apple Watch knows about you throughout the day.

Most importantly, Apple isn't just increasing the frequency of heart rate readings and pushing the burden of interpreting data onto the user. The new hardware, combined with watchOS 27, provides meaningful insights into your life, including the promising Ready app and a more powerful Vitals app.

If you factor in the Siri Recap and Live Rewind features coming later this year, the story gets even more exciting. Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 not only know you better than ever, but will also help you keep up with the world around you.

Overall, Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 provide the clearest indication yet of the future of Apple's most important wearable.

My top Apple Watch recommendations:

  • Apple Watch Series 12
  • Twelve South Butterfly 2-in-1
  • Anker 3-in-1 charging stand (for iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch)
  • Nomad Titanium Apple Watch Band
  • My favorite Apple Watch bands
